doc.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021

title: The New York work scene
summary: He describes New York as vibrant and competitive, with endless jam sessions that keep standards high.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Let’s suppose this question I’m going to ask was asked like 14 months ago. What is the work scene like generally in New York now.
You’re asking this for 14 months ago?
Yes. Like I’m pretending that the pandemic did not happen.

Well New York City is great. What could possibly ever go wrong? It’s going to be like this forever, Monk. Well the New York scene is really vibrant. It’s a place that even after 12 years continues to inspire me. There’s just so much music here, there’s so many opportunities to hear music and to play you know. There’s so many jam sessions you can go to up ‘til two, three in the morning you know. It just never ceases to be inspiring you know. And it makes me competitive in a good way. It makes me think okay I can’t relax because there’s so many great players here, like I heard this guy play this tune, I need to learn that better. And there’s no other place in the world that I’ve felt like that, that I really felt like I’ve got to get my act together because these guys are serious players you know. And that’s the great thing about this scene, it’s just overwhelming, the amount of great players here. But that’s what keeps the level so high.
